Q: Can a PWA schedule notifications when closed? A:

Short answer: not reliably, and on iOS not at all.

What the web platform gives you today:

  • Push API works when the page is closed, but it requires a server to send the push — there is no "schedule locally for 8:00" in it.

  • Notification Triggers API (showTrigger: new TimestampTrigger(...)) was exactly this feature, but it never left Chrome's origin trial and is abandoned — it does not work in current browsers.

  • setTimeout + new Notification(...) dies as soon as the tab is throttled or closed; on mobile that happens within seconds of the screen turning off.

  • On iOS, web push exists since 16.4 for installed PWAs, but again only server-sent push — no local scheduling.

So a PWA cannot ring an alarm at an exact time with the app closed unless you run a push server and accept push delivery semantics (which are best-effort, not exact-time).

If your real requirement is "a single HTML file that fires an exact alarm on a phone", the practical options are: wrap it yourself (Capacitor/Cordova + local-notifications plugin gives you AlarmManager exact alarms on Android and UNCalendarNotificationTrigger on iOS), or use a runner app that does the wrapping for you. I built one of those — Kapsula (kapsula.app, I'm the author): it runs a single HTML file in a sandboxed WebView and exposes kapsula.notify.schedule({at, title, body}), which is a real OS alarm that fires with the app closed. The same file still works unchanged in a desktop browser if you guard the calls with if (window.kapsula).

Either way the key point is: the scheduling has to live in the OS notification system, not in JavaScript timers — the browser will never keep your timer alive with the screen off.

Q: Is there an opposite method of "in?" in Rails? A:

No, opposite method does not exist. But you can write it yourself. Something like:

create file object.rb in your project (like this lib/core_ext/object.rb):

# frozen_string_literal: true

module CoreExt
  module Object
    # Returns true if this object is included in the argument. Argument must be
    # any object which responds to +#include?+. Usage:
    #
    #   characters = ["Konata", "Kagami", "Tsukasa"]
    #   "Konata".in?(characters) # => true
    #   "Hiragi".out?(characters) # => true
    #
    def out?(another_object)
      !in?(another_object)
    end
  end
end

Then you must add this module to app loading.

For example, let's create new initializer (like this your_app/config/initializers/core_ext.rb)

# frozen_string_literal: true

Rails.application.config.to_prepare do
  Object.include CoreExt::Object
end

And then in your case

4.out([1,2,3])?  => true

Q: How can I solve a string ambiguity? A:

The problem arises beacuse of lexer ambivalence between INT and DIR, as both the lexer rules could match a numeric value such as 28566 or 007. Switching the order of the rules will solve one case but not the other.

The appropriate solution to this problem will be to delete the conflicting lexer rules of INT and DIR and use the single rule of the token named VALUE. Then using the parser context we can determine if the value is a port or a directory.

For instance:

connect port=28566 --> VALUE("28566")
cd 007 --> VALUE("007")

Thus, the solution to this problem will be to use VALUE: [a-zA-Z0-9_/.]+; and validate the port value independently when parsing the connect command.

Q: Error Code 0x84BB0001 when installing SQL Server 2016 A:

I realise this is an old post, but I recently struck this issue as I needed to install 2016 for vendor compatibility.

In my case the issue was the service accounts being used.

Solution was to install using the default NT Service virtual accounts then change to domain accounts post install (we were actually using group managed service accounts)

Q: How to discard a message from inside a MessageConverter A:

The converter should not return Optional.empty(). The converter should throw MessageConversionException for a message which cannot/should not be converted and the ConditionalRejectingErrorHandler will reject it without requeue. This ensures that conversion and message disposition are separated.

Q: OPENROWSET copying tables between databases on the same server A:

For one thing: Your OPENROWSET statement isn't specifying the server instance.

Try

SELECT *
FROM OPENROWSET(
    'MSOLEDBSQL',
    'Server=DB-SANDINT\SAND;Trusted_Connection=Yes;',
    'SELECT * FROM db2.dbo.myTable(nolock)'
);

and for "Ad Hoc Distributed Queries" Erros, Try

EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1
RECONFIGURE

EXEC sp_configure 'Ad Hoc Distributed Queries', 1
RECONFIGURE
